title: openalex_W7215913570
universal_lens: Reinforcement learning agents in vision-based environments benefit from optical flow integration to enhance motion representation and cumulative reward maximization. A unified framework integrating grayscale image states I(t) with optical flow v(t) as a composite input for Deep Q-Networks, enabling motion-aware reinforcement learning via spatiotemporal feature concatenation.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference of agent policies using conformal predictive distributions over visual and motion features for robust decision-making under uncertainty. Bayesian inference over concatenated visual-optical flow states enables probabilistic action selection under uncertainty; conformal prediction bounds model confidence in policy decisions.
gse_mapping: Situationally aware state transitions in Atari environments are modeled via optical flow-enhanced CNN inputs to guide action selection and reward optimization. Situational reasoning maps I(t) and v(t) into transition graphs capturing agent dynamics; state transitions encode motion semantics for predictive planning in Atari environments.

primitives.name: Optical Flow Motion Representation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Optical flow (OF) gives information about the motion in sequential image data such as videos, which makes it useful in reinforcement learning.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'OF': 'dimensionless, represents pixel displacement per time unit'}
primitives.assumptions: Motion in video sequences can be approximated as local pixel displacement vectors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When motion is sparse or occlusions dominate, optical flow becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Optical flow vector fields are isomorphic to velocity fields in dynamical systems, enabling RL agents to infer environmental dynamics from visual motion cues.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual optical flow vectors during training.

primitives.name: Deep Q-Network Enhancement with Motion Cues
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our experiments show that adding OF to an environment improves the training of the Deep Q Network (DQN) model and shows higher rewards compared to concatenating the present frame with its previous frame.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{t}': 'reward scalar at time t', 'Q(s,a)': 'Q-value function for state-action pair'}
primitives.assumptions: The addition of optical flow increases the signal-to-noise ratio in state representations for DQN.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When reward signals are sparse or delayed, motion cues may not sufficiently improve learning.

layer2.mapping: The kernel of enhanced DQN policy updates incorporates optical flow as a derived feature space, improving convergence speed and reward accumulation.
layer2.telemetry: Average reward per episode normalized by training steps across multiple runs.

primitives.name: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: The need for understanding the dynamics of an environment led to the advent of model-based RL (MBRL).
primitives.assumptions: Environment dynamics can be accurately modeled to enable planning and policy improvement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When true dynamics are highly stochastic or non-Markovian, MBRL fails to generalize effectively.

layer2.mapping: MBRL frameworks are isomorphic to probabilistic graphical models where state transitions are encoded as conditional distributions, allowing for symbolic reasoning over latent variables.
layer2.telemetry: Prediction accuracy of next-state distributions against ground truth in simulated rollouts.

primitives.name: Visual Reinforcement Learning Agent
primitives.verbatim_quote: In visual RL, agents must learn actions that maximize a notion of cumulative reward based on visual observations of the environment.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_{t}': 'visual observation at time t (image tensor)', 'A_{t}': 'action taken at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Visual inputs contain sufficient information to infer environmental structure and reward opportunities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When visual input lacks discriminative features or is corrupted by noise, agent performance degrades significantly.

layer2.mapping: The kernel of visual RL policies is derived from convolutional feature maps augmented with optical flow, forming a hybrid sensory state space for action selection.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of policy execution in Atari games after training with visual and motion inputs.

primitives.name: Optical Flow Augmented State Encoding
primitives.verbatim_quote: In our paper, the states will be grayscaled and rescaled images at time t, I(t), concatenated with its optical flow.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I(t)': 'grayscale image tensor, 84×84×1 pixels', 'v(t)': 'optical flow vector field, 84×84×2 pixels', 's(t)': 'concatenated state tensor, 84×84×3 pixels'}
primitives.assumptions: Images are preprocessed to fixed resolution; optical flow captures local motion dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When optical flow magnitude exceeds threshold, motion dominates visual features.

layer2.mapping: State space is isomorphic to a product manifold of image and motion spaces, enabling joint representation learning.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual optical flow vectors.

primitives.name: Lucas-Kanade Optical Flow Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: We grayscale the frame and resize it to 84×84 to obtain I(t) For I(t), we compute the OF v(t) using the Lucas–Kanade method.
primitives.latex: \mathbf{v}(t) = \arg\min_{\mathbf{v}} \sum_{x,y} \left( I(x+\Delta x, y+\Delta y, t+1) - I(x, y, t) - \nabla I \cdot \mathbf{v} \right)^2
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I(x, y, t)': 'intensity value at pixel (x, y) at time t', '\\mathbf{v}(t)': 'optical flow vector at time t', '\\nabla I': 'spatial gradient of intensity'}
primitives.assumptions: Brightness constancy assumption holds locally; small motion between frames.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Large motion or illumination changes cause estimation failure.

layer2.mapping: Kernel computes spatial gradients and temporal differences to estimate velocity fields.

primitives.name: Optical Flow Normalization for DQN Compatibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: For compatibility with DQN, we scaled the OF by: v(t) ← np.uint8(np.clip(8v(t) + 127.5,0,255)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v(t)': 'raw optical flow values', "v'(t)": 'scaled optical flow for uint8 encoding'}
primitives.assumptions: DQN requires discrete integer inputs; scaling preserves relative motion magnitude.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Clipping introduces saturation when flow exceeds ±31.875.

layer2.mapping: Linear transformation maps continuous optical flow to discrete 8-bit range suitable for neural network input.
layer2.telemetry: Histogram entropy of scaled optical flow channels.

primitives.name: Concatenated Visual-Motion State Tensor
primitives.verbatim_quote: We then concatenate I(t) with v(t) to obtain the state st ∈R3×84×84, which we then pass into our DQN as input.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I(t)': 'grayscale image tensor', 'v(t)': 'scaled optical flow tensor', 's(t)': 'combined state tensor'}
primitives.assumptions: Temporal alignment of image and flow tensors; channel-wise concatenation preserves modality separation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Misalignment of I(t) and v(t) leads to degraded performance due to misinterpreted motion cues.

layer2.mapping: Tensor product structure allows joint convolutional processing across both visual and motion modalities.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-correlation between concatenated state components and reward signal.

Chapter 1 introduces the foundational tension in reinforcement learning: how to extract meaningful motion cues from visual data to inform decision-making. The core thesis hinges on integrating optical flow into standard CNN architectures for Atari environments, thereby enhancing the agent's ability to perceive temporal dynamics. This approach aligns with the broader paradigm shift towards incorporating structured motion information in deep RL models. The motivation stems from the limitation of static frame analysis, which fails to capture dynamic changes essential for high-performing agents. By concatenating optical flow with raw image frames, the system gains access to both spatial and temporal gradients, enabling more informed policy updates. This dual-input strategy is particularly beneficial in environments with fast-moving objects or complex interactions, where motion provides critical contextual signals. The theoretical grounding lies in the principle that motion encodes environmental dynamics, which is central to model-free and model-based approaches alike. The Dyna framework and Monte Carlo Tree Search exemplify prior efforts to incorporate environmental models, but they often rely on explicit modeling rather than implicit feature extraction. Here, optical flow serves as a proxy for motion dynamics, bridging the gap between perception and action in vision-based RL. The empirical validation via DQN improvements underscores the practical utility of this integration. Thus, the chapter sets up a methodological framework that combines classical computer vision techniques with modern deep learning paradigms to advance agent intelligence in sequential decision-making domains.
